I re-ran both arms independently: at head 3fb07d05 the four tests pass (4 passed, EXIT=0) and at base 3dfed112, with the head test file present and the two source files reverted, the same four tests fail (4 failed, EXIT=1). No test that passes at head fails at base, so the run added no failures. findings.text: follow-on: the operator-visible pending-enrich count is not covered by the set-aside exclusion. get_discovery_stats (frontier.py:260) computes enrichment_ready from (should_enrich=true OR scan_relevance>=minimum) AND (is_enriched NULL/false) with no coalesce(enrich_set_aside,false)=false clause; that value is assigned to state.pending_enrich at progress.py:1247 and rendered in the discovery progress panel (progress.py:762). So after this change the paths stage terminates correctly (has_pending_work is fixed) but the display still reports a nonzero enrich backlog from the set-aside paths -- the exact confusing symptom the plan describes, left on the display surface. frontier.py is outside this node's write paths, so it is a follow-on rather than a defect in this node.

follow-on: get_paths_pending_enrichment (enrichment.py:584, inside this node's declared write scope) still selects paths with (is_enriched NULL/false AND (should_enrich=true OR (should_enrich IS NULL AND scan_relevance>=threshold))) and no set-aside exclusion, so a set-aside path is returned again here. It is reachable only through run_enrichment_pipeline (enrichment.py:618), which currently has no callers in the package, so the gap is latent rather than live; it should carry the same coalesce(enrich_set_aside,false)=false clause as parallel.py for consistency and to avoid the bug reappearing if that pipeline is re-wired.

follow-on: the former timeout branch that recovered partial enrichment output was removed, not migrated. The two call sites (sync enrich_paths ~line 282 and async async_enrich_paths ~line 509) previously caught subprocess.TimeoutExpired and, when the exception carried partial stdout, parsed the completed JSONL lines and persisted them via _parse_enrich_output; a timeout with no partial output became a per-path ssh_timeout error. That branch is gone, and an unhandled timeout now flows to the generic handler where _host_unreachable(e) is True (TimeoutExpired), so the whole batch re-raises, the claims are reverted and the worker pauses. The executor does populate partial output (executor.py:1349 sets exc.output from the killed process's stdout), so a reachable-but-slow host now loses its already-completed partial results on every retry instead of persisting them, and _wait_for_reachable_host returns immediately when SSH is healthy, so such a host loops on backoff discarding partial work. This is a behaviour change beyond the plan's wording and is not covered by the added tests (the timeout case only asserts the pause).

follow-on: the reviewed manifest leaves both structured gate-arm fields empty -- baseline_suite (line 21) and after_suite (line 22) carry no JSON -- so a reader deriving the added-failure set from the manifest's own machine-readable arms finds nothing and must fall back to the free-text test_logs. The arms exist as files (baseline-path-enrich-corrected.log, head-path-enrich.log) and I used them, so the run added no failures, but the empty fields are the defect the derivation contract is written to prevent.

follow-on: the unreachability classifier and its backoff still live in imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py (_host_unreachable, _wait_for_reachable_host) and the paths stage imports them privately across the subsystem boundary. Plan section 63 names this exact state: the 2026-10-09 node may import them from the code scan, and a follow-on node moves them into a module both stages import and repoints both callers. The node correctly avoided a second copy, but the shared-owner move remains outstanding and should be dispatched.

justifications.durability: each of the three done-when behaviours is guarded by a test I confirmed reddens at base and greens at head: the unreachable pause test fails at base with waits==[] and asserts no persistence at head; the set-aside test fails at base with failures 0==1 and passes at head; the pending-count test fails at base with has_pending_work True and passes at head. The reviewed run's negative control (removing the per-path counter in a scratch copy) reddens the set-aside test with 0==1, so the guard fires. The residual weakness is that the two reachable-failure tests mock GraphClient with a string-matching PathGraph, so a Cypher-level regression (a renamed property or a syntax error) would not be caught by them; no -m graph test exercises mark_enrichment_complete's error branch, and the base-arm reproduction I ran is the strongest available evidence that the guard is not vacuous.
justifications.evidence: the base arm (4 failed, EXIT=1 at 3dfed112) and the head arm (4 passed, EXIT=0 at 3fb07d05) are recorded and I reproduced both independently; the related gate (102 passed) is recorded but its header names the working tree rather than the committed head, and the new tests mock the graph rather than exercising the real Cypher, so the evidence is solid for the unit behaviour and thinner for the query correctness.
justifications.fit: the change follows the code-scan idiom the plan names and reuses its classifier/backoff instead of duplicating them, and it introduces no plan, sprint or version label (ENRICH_FAILURE_LIMIT, enrich_failures, enrich_set_aside, unreachable_count are all mechanism-named). The two deductions are that it imports private helpers across the subsystem boundary (sanctioned pending the deferred move) and that it silently dropped the timeout partial-output recovery, a behaviour change the plan did not ask for and no test covers.
justifications.goal_fidelity: parallel.py:1064-1098 implements the increment-and-set-aside and the succeed-resets branch, parallel.py:307/425/852 thread the exclusion into the three reachable pending/claim queries, and enrichment.py re-raises on an unreachable host so the worker pauses; every plan done-when is delivered and tested. The only part of section 63 not done is the shared-owner move, which the plan itself defers to a follow-on node for the 2026-10-09 dispatch.
justifications.reuse: the node reused the existing _host_unreachable and _wait_for_reachable_host rather than writing a second copy, which is the non-duplicating choice the plan requires; the remaining cost is the private cross-subsystem import that the deferred follow-on node is to replace with a shared module, so the reuse is correct but not yet at its intended resting point.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff against 3dfed112 is the three declared paths and nothing else; no shared index, sprint state or other plan files were touched.
